cards.explanation: The answer is to go show love to her again. The LORD says, “Go show love to your wife again…” (Hosea 3:1). Look at that word again, friends. She is loved by another, and the LORD still sends Hosea to love her. I think that's a big ask, and Hosea is the one telling us about it.

The answer is gods. The LORD says to love her “…as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods…” (Hosea 3:1). That's the comparison, friends. The Israelites turn to other gods, and the LORD loves them anyway.

The answer is that he buys her back. Hosea says, “So I bought her for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a lethech of barley.” (Hosea 3:2). Silver and barley, friends, so no coupons. Not even the expired coupon I shared a junk drawer with would have covered this one.

The answer is belong to another. Hosea tells her, “You must live with me for many days; you must not be promiscuous or belong to another…” (Hosea 3:3). Living with him and not belonging to another go together in that line, friends. That's what he asks of her.

The answer is False. Hosea tells her what to do, and then he adds, “…and I will do the same for you.” (Hosea 3:3). So he does make a promise of his own, friends. It isn't a one-way deal, because he's in it with her.

The answer is a king or a prince. Hosea says the Israelites “…must live many days without king or prince…” (Hosea 3:4). Picture a job site with no boss and no manager, friends. Nobody even to ask where the extension cord went.

The answer is False. Hosea says the Israelites “must live many days… without ephod or idol.” (Hosea 3:4). So Israel will not still have its ephod and its idols, friends. Both are gone from the picture, and the idols are on the list of things they'll go without.

The answer is True. Hosea says, “Afterward, the people of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God…” (Hosea 3:5). Look at that word afterward, friends. The many days don't get the last word, and that's good news.

The answer is His goodness. Hosea says, “They will come trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the last days.” (Hosea 3:5). The text puts goodness right next to the trembling, friends. And this is the last thing Hosea says in the passage.
